identification: Mixed lot of about 17 pieces, mostly green Depression-era (1930s) uranium glass kitchenware plus a few Victorian pieces. Pieces: (1) large clear-green ruffled bowl with radiating ribs and star-cut base, c.25-30 cm; (2) Victorian apricot/peach ribbed vase or spill with opal (white) swirl threading and rope-twist rim on applied crimped green uranium leaf feet (English, Stourbridge type, c.1880-1900); (3) Victorian apricot/peach iridescent tall bud vase with applied green/vaseline trailing (base area cloudy); (4) Victorian vaseline opalescent bell-shaped light shade or epergne-type piece with crimped/ruffled rim (yellow vaseline with opal); (5) jadeite (opaque jade-green milk glass) handled reamer; (6) jadeite handled cup/large mug; (7) green uranium 2-cup measuring jug with graduations (Hazel Atlas / Kellogg's type, 3-spout style, markings not legible); (8) green uranium handled lemon reamer; (9) separate green reamer cone top; (10) green rectangular refrigerator/loaf/butter dish with ribbed fan panels; (11) large green art deco 3-footed oval dish/bowl (English, Sowerby/Bagley/Davidson type); (12) brighter mint-green 2-handled bowl with cross-hatch panels and central rosette (tab handles); (13) green footed sherbet/compote with moulded fan base; (14) small green art deco footed vase/sugar with stepped panels; (15) small green ribbed creamer/jug; (16) small yellow vaseline egg cup. Catalogue says some pieces as is.

viewing_check: Check the Victorian vase feet and rope rim for chips, the vaseline shade rim for chips/cracks (crimped rims chip easily), the bud vase base, and look for Fire-King/McKee/Sunkist marks under the jadeite reamer and Hazel Atlas/Federal marks under the measuring jug. A UV torch confirms which pieces glow.
